changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For subscription and membership businesses, lead with this in place of the global opener: "Win back members who never meant to leave." Back it with a recovery analysis of one month of the prospect's own failed renewals, showing which ones usually come back with a retry or an updated card. Use their file, not our average, and frame it as involuntary churn in the terms they report to their board. Do not quote a share of churn until we have a verified number.
changes.why: The evaluation started when Corelane split board-reported churn into cancellations and failed cards ("members who never meant to leave"), and the deal was signed four days after Tobi ran a recovery analysis on their own failed renewals.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For regional subscription businesses (e.g. a US and Canada gym chain), stop opening with the global, every-currency line. Open with their failed renewals and involuntary churn instead (see the M10 change).
changes.why: The rep opened with the global slide to a US-and-Canada chain and got silence.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For studio and gym verticals, until we can demo our reader live inside the customer's studio software: "Start with online membership billing now. Front-desk card readers in your studio software come in phase two, delivered through our partner integration." Use plain front-desk language (readers, one screen at the front desk), not "unified commerce."
changes.why: The buyer translated 'unified commerce' into "is that the readers?", we couldn't show the reader live in their studio software ("the studio managers will revolt" at two screens), and in-store stayed with the incumbent, undated and dependent on the partner.

changes.change: For the finance buyer (controller or CFO) at subscription businesses, add a proof point: "A business case built on your own failed renewals, plus a plain answer on contract term, switching cost and exit fees." Put it in front of the person who signs early, labelled as a business case, not a demo, rather than relying on the champion to carry it.
changes.why: The controller who signed sat on the paper for two weeks and stayed silent until he asked to keep the customer-data spreadsheet, and the buying questions turned to contract term and what it costs to get out.
